title: Cache density -> Savings phaseplane (sensitivity sweep)
content:
Purpose:
This sheet explores an alternative decomposition for KV/prefix cache impact called a 'phaseplane' sweep: instead of only looking at hit-rate vs. cost, we sweep cache density (fraction of distinct prefix space stored) against sequence overlap (effective reuse coefficient) and show end-to-end $ savings and tail-latency risk. The goal is to give product + infra a quick lookup for which density/overlap combinations are high ROI and which require engineering investment (prefetch, cold-probe, per-tenant residency).

Quick summary of approach (high level):
- Define a small set of input knobs: cache_density (0..1), overlap_coeff (0..1), eviction_churn (0..1), cold_fraction (0..1), burst_index (1..5).
- Derive effective_hit_rate ≈ cache_density * overlap_coeff * (1 - eviction_churn) * (1 - cold_fraction). This is intentionally simple to be interpretable in a phaseplane.
- Map effective_hit_rate to per-token cost multiplier via model of batching & KV-lookup overhead: token_cost = baseline_token_cost * (1 - effective_hit_rate * batching_efficiency).
- Estimate per-100k-requests savings and compute expected tail q95 latency penalty scenarios when hit rate drops.

Assumptions (placeholders — change per-customer):
- baseline_token_cost = $0.00060 per token served (includes GPU + infra amortized)
- average_tokens_per_request = 240 (prompt+generation)
- batching_efficiency = 0.55 (effective reduction in per-token cost when cache hit avoids full model generation or short-circuits tokens)
- baseline_q95_latency = 320ms; cache-hit q95 latency improvement = 0.65x (short-circuit + smaller KV decode)
- eviction_churn driven by tenant fragmentation; 0.2 is moderate churn
- cold_fraction = fraction of sessions with unique prefixes (e.g., new sessions), 0.3 default
- burst_index multiplies request variance and affects warmup penalty sizing

Phaseplane grid (how to read):
- X axis = cache_density (0.05 increments, 0.05..0.9) => fraction of hot prefix space stored
- Y axis = overlap_coeff (0.1..1.0) => how often incoming sequences reuse stored prefixes
- Each cell returns: effective_hit_rate, estimated $ savings per 100k requests, estimated q95 latency change (ms), sensitivity_flag (low/med/high).

Representative calculation example (cell):
Inputs: cache_density=0.4, overlap_coeff=0.6, eviction_churn=0.15, cold_fraction=0.25, burst_index=1.8
effective_hit_rate = 0.4 * 0.6 * (1 - 0.15) * (1 - 0.25) = 0.4 * 0.6 * 0.85 * 0.75 ≈ 0.153
per-token cost multiplier = 1 - effective_hit_rate * batching_efficiency = 1 - 0.153 * 0.55 ≈ 0.9158
per-request token cost = baseline_token_cost * avg_tokens * multiplier = 0.0006 * 240 * 0.9158 ≈ $0.1322
baseline per-request = 0.0006 * 240 = $0.1440 => savings per request ≈ $0.0118 => per 100k requests ≈ $1,180
q95 latency: baseline 320ms * (1 - 0.153 * 0.35) ≈ 320 * 0.9465 ≈ 303ms (approx 17ms improvement)
Sensitivity classification: if small delta in cache_density (±0.05) changes savings by >15% => high sensitivity. For this cell delta is ~8% => medium.

Sample table (first 3 rows of X=0.1..0.25; Y=0.2..0.8 shown collapsed):
| cache_density | overlap_coeff | eff_hit_rate | $/100k reqs | q95_ms | sensitivity | notes |
| 0.10 | 0.20 | 0.012 | $86 | 318 | high | very sparse density + low overlap -> almost no ROI; engineering not justified unless overlap increases |
| 0.18 | 0.40 | 0.046 | $395 | 312 | med | modest wins if eviction_churn reduced by 0.05 |
| 0.25 | 0.70 | 0.118 | $1,015 | 306 | low | good sweet spot for per-tenant residency investment |

Edgecases and anomalies we've observed in customer traces (notes):
- Long-tail prompts with personal identifiers produce effective overlap_coeff near 0 — prefix caching gives negligible wins but can still help prefix-compressed embedding cache.
- Very bursty telemetry (burst_index > 3) amplifies warmup costs; small densities give negative ROI when burst_index grows because warm-start probes dominate.
- Multi-tenant co-location increases eviction_churn nonlinearly as active tenants grow; a per-tenant residency filter can massively improve effective_hit_rate at modest memory cost.

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-up sweeps):
- Replace simple multiplicative effective_hit_rate with empirically-fit logistic model per-customer trace. (linked OPT-412).
- Add a separate table for prefix-size distribution impact (small vs large prefixes change memory dynamics).
- Iterate with infra to add measured q95 improvements when cache hit avoids model fetch vs short token generation (currently heuristic).
- Run phaseplane per-model-size (7B/13B/70B) — batching efficiency differs substantially.

Actionable recommendations (current):
- If customer shows overlap_coeff >= 0.5 at cache_density >= 0.2 => recommend low-effort: enable 7-day per-tenant residency + eviction softening; expected payback in 6–9 weeks for mid-size customers.
- If overlap_coeff < 0.2 and burst_index > 2 => do not prioritize prefix cache; instead focus on request coalescing and probe-prefetch strategies.
- For customers with high eviction_churn (>=0.3), prototype per-tenant pinned segments before global cache growth.

Notes-to-self / loose links in this doc:
- Quick script used to generate grid lives in /repos/optimize/sim/phaseplane-sim.py (ask Miguel for a copy).
- Customer traces sampled: CUST-A (conversational, high reuse), CUST-D (search-like, low reuse). See OPT-412 for trace IDs.

Appendix: quick sensitivity checklist for SRE/product when reviewing customer config:
- Is per-tenant residency enabled? (Y/N)
- Median prefix length and stddev (bytes)
- Observed q95 on cold sessions (ms)
- Cache eviction rate per hour
- Peak concurrency and burst multiplier
